column3: “Perfect faithfulness” combines the two concluding expressions for faithfulness and firmness.
“The cities” is singular in the Hebrew: a city.
“Cools the heat” makes explicit the comparison between heat and the shade of a cloud.
“Choice meat” does not explicitly retain the description of the rich food as full of marrow; the wine is described as wine on the lees, strained.
“His pride will be brought low” recasts an active verb as passive; “despite” replaces “with” in the phrase about the skill of his hands.
The Hebrew addresses “your walls”; the translation omits the possessive and renders the sequence of active verbs passively.
